title: Bound till the Thaw

owner_instructions: Where: the line 'Meera did not think about the rest of what she carried, and she was good at not thinking about it.' What's wrong: Meera's own POV knows she is the Salt Fox, and this line hides it from the reader. That is the 'Contrived delays' failure mode, and it is the likely reason chapter 1 scores lowest of the opening. What to change: cut the coy line. In its place, give Meera one short, plain line that owns the crew name and its price. Put it at the village gate, at the Closing Law notice and the hanging tree with its two fresh pegs. For example, she knows which name those empty pegs are waiting for: the Salt Fox, hers. Keep it to one or two sentences of interiority that turn into action, such as looking away, counting, or walking on. Do not let it become rumination.

Where: anywhere else in the chapter where Meera's narration dances around the crew name or her role. What to change: once the hanging-tree line is in place, remove any further hedging that pretends she doesn't know. She keeps the secret from other people, not from herself or the reader.

Keep unchanged: the opening count ('Nine. Ten. Eleven.'), the scraped crate lid, the brass button sewn into the ledger spine, Meera's age (29) and Rohan's 'about thirty-five' on the page, Rohan's line 'It is a goat, and it has not been charged with anything', and 'Then you will do. Guide.'

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: any Meera interiority that dodges or veils her identity as the Salt Fox, for example while she sizes up Rohan or Varun. What to change: if her thoughts hide the name from the reader, let her name it plainly and briefly in her own head. She still says nothing aloud. If there is no such dodge, make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: the first trade of questions, when Rohan says he hunts the crew because a warden died on the pass. What to change: if Meera's interiority veils the fact that the crew he hunts is hers, let her register it plainly in one line, as dread rather than mystery. If there is no veiling, make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: the moment Rohan asks her not to show him anything he would have to report, before she shows him the crew ledge. What to change: if her narration coyly withholds why the ledge is dangerous for her personally, state it plainly in her head. It is her crew's ledge and she is the Salt Fox. Keep it to one line. Otherwise make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: Meera's interiority in the Rope-Hut, especially around 'this fire is harbouring' and the crown-grade redbark. What to change: remove any line that hides her Salt Fox identity from the reader. If there is none, make no change.

Cross-check for chapter 30. Note whether Rohan swears in verse while climbing out of the crevasse or snow bridge in the haul-out. Chapter 30's 'since you climbed out of that gully swearing in verse' must match a moment that is actually on the page. Do not add a new swearing moment here just to fit chapter 30; fix chapter 30 instead.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: the parley with Asha and the evening questions. What to change: if Meera's narration veils that she is the Salt Fox in a way that hides a fact the reader should already own, replace the veiling with a plain line of dread. Otherwise make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: Meera holding the seal and weighing a pardon for her crew from Asha. What to change: if her reasoning avoids naming the fact that the hanging name is hers, let her name it plainly. The refusal costs more when the reader knows exactly whose neck the pardon would save. Otherwise make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: 'The double price is in no record' / 'Nobody writes down what we do for free.' What to change: if any surrounding interiority coyly withholds that she is the Salt Fox, make it plain in one line. Otherwise make no change.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: the near-kiss and 'At the thaw you deliver me. I don't kiss my noose.' What to change: make sure the interiority around this line treats her identity as known to the reader. 'You deliver me' should read as a fact she has carried since chapter 1, not as a hint. Remove any veiling. Otherwise make no change.

Where: the Varun deduction sequence, which runs through the sieve ring, button, gully, iron ring, Lalit's number, the fallback and the seal. What's wrong: it is a long back-and-forth of evidence that slows the midpoint. What to change: build the deduction on three clinching facts only. These are the brass button, Lalit's 'three wardens' (the approach numbers only the plan held), and the fallback route only Rohan and Varun drew. The other clues still need to stay retrievable for fair play: the scraped stamps (C01), the gully 'safer' route (C04), the double crack and Varun lagging (C05), the sieve mark (C07) and the hunter's redbark (C15). Compress them into one fast line, or a single shared glance, rather than debating each one.

Where: the line 'It's Varun. It was always Varun.' What's wrong: it tells the reader a conclusion the evidence has already delivered. What to change: cut it. Do not replace it with another summary line. End the deduction on the two twists lying side by side on the stone, her silver funding Pritam and his trust in Jassi's killer, and let the silence carry it. Remember that silence is free.

Where: Rohan's dialogue in this chapter, including 'It would appear so,' 'I do not say it for pardon,' and 'That is no small thing to share.' What's wrong: the formal, no-contraction legal cadence stacks up until he sounds like a deposition. What to change: rewrite at least two of these three lines so they are shorter, plainer, or more physical, while he still sounds like Rohan. Keep his no-contraction signature where it bites.

Consistency with the chapter 1 Salt Fox change. Where: the build-up to 'I am the Salt Fox.' What to change: the reader has known since chapter 1. Frame the beat as a confession Meera dreads making to him, priced in sticks, heat and the hanging tree, and not as information revealed to the reader. Remove any narration that treats the name as a surprise.

Keep unchanged: 'I suspected and I chose not to know. That is not the same as ignorance, but it is not far from it.'; 'He kissed like a man reading a document he had waited a long time to sign'; 'That was free.' / 'I know. I watched your hands.'; and the promise 'I will not let you fall on this mountain' with the rope's hum.

continuity_fixes: Ch17 says that for ten days Rohan took the downhill place on the rope and went first through every door. In fact he walked in her steps behind her (ch3, ch4, ch7) and she entered the hut first (ch8). FIX: Make it a habit he kept reaching for and she kept stopping.

The countdown to the Snow Fair contradicts the events and the twenty-day frame. Chapter 6 gives seventeen days left at dawn of day 4, and chapter 29 has the Fair at the dawn of day twenty. Chapter 13 (day 9) says nine days are left. Chapter 19 (day 12) says four. Chapter 21 says three, and chapter 22 says two. Chapter 23 says the snow day forces them to push through to arrive on the Fair morning even if they leave the next dawn. Yet Varun delays them a further day, they walk a day and a night, and they still arrive while the investiture is under way. FIX: Make the Fair fall on day twenty throughout. Kiran sleeps two days, so ch21 opens on day 15. Restate the days left at each point. Ch21's one-day concession leaves one spare day, the snow takes it, and Varun's day forces the night push to reach the meadow.
owner_instructions: Consistency check for chapter 32's bell fix. Where: Sunni's burial. What to change: make sure the page shows Jassi's small kid bell going into Sunni's grave, in one clear concrete line naming whose bell it was. Chapter 32 relies on this. If it is already clear on the page, make no change.

Verification only, for the chapter 30 age-line cut. Make sure both leads' ages (29 and 35) are on the page before the open-door scene, as the outline requires. If they are present, make no change. If they are missing, add them naturally, for example through the count, a winters-of-service detail, or dialogue. Do not use a compliance-style line.

continuity_fixes: In ch 1 the brass button token was stitched into the ledger's spine 'where only a person who unpicked the binding would find it'. In ch 28 it simply comes out when Meera reaches in with two fingers. FIX: Have her pick the stitches to free it.

owner_instructions: Where: 'We're twenty-nine and thirty-five, and I want to be very clear that I am not asking leave of anybody.' What's wrong: it reads like a compliance box. The ages are already on the page in chapters 1, 2 and 20, so the adults-only rule is met. What to change: cut the ages and keep the defiance, as in 'I'm not asking leave of anybody.'

Where: 'since you climbed out of that gully swearing in verse.' What's wrong: it may point to a moment that is not on the page, or to the wrong place. What to change: check chapters 3, 7 and 8. If he swore in verse climbing out of the crevasse or snow bridge in the chapter 8 haul-out, change 'gully' to 'crevasse'. If the swearing happened in the chapter 3 gully avalanche, keep 'gully'. If no such moment exists anywhere, rewrite the callback to a moment that does exist, such as climbing on her count with his ribs screaming.

Where: the italic line *A law is a rope, she thought. It depends who ties it.*, placed just before Meera steps forward to confess. What's wrong: it tells the reader the meaning before the act delivers it. What to change: remove it from before the confession. Let the act land first: she steps up and enters the count under 'Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox.' Then deliver the line either after the herald writes her name, or aloud to Rohan on the wall afterwards. Speaking it to him is preferred, because dialogue does the work. Use it once only.
Keep unchanged: the 'Watch my hands' declaration with bare, warm hands, and her three remaining left fingers staying warm. Do not signpost the callback.

Where: Ila's 'A bound rope is not "about twelve arm-spans"' and Rohan's 'The jogini refuse anything longer.' What's wrong: every other chapter, chapter 32 and the blurb say eight arm-spans. What to change: make it eight. Keep Ila's precision joke, for example by correcting someone's 'about eight' to exactly eight. Check every other distance in the drafting scene for the same error.

Where: Rohan's 'I will not hand you to anyone,' with the rope humming low and level. What's wrong: by the mountain's rule that is a binding promise. It answers chapter 32's question a chapter early and drains the cairn scene of suspense. It also breaks Rohan's established refusal to promise what he cannot guarantee (chapters 6, 20 and 23). What to change: turn it into an intent he will not dress up as a promise, along the lines of 'I have not found how to make the paper say no. I am looking.' Remove the rope's hum entirely. Then show Meera noticing that he did not promise. This is Rohan's POV, so show it through her action or dialogue, for example a dry 'That isn't a promise' or a look at the silent rope. Give him a brief, honest reply.

Keep unchanged: the amputation count, with 206 people carried and then 'Two hundred and seven'; the felted glove cut for a thumb and three fingers; Kiran in the room for the 'no one hangs for a death on a bound crossing' clause; and the closed-door 'Stay.'

Consistency with the chapter 31 promise change. Where: before and during the senior warden Gopal raising the writ at the cairn. What to change: chapter 31 no longer contains a binding promise. Make sure nothing here refers to a hum or a promise from chapter 31. Give Meera a short beat of real uncertainty before Rohan answers: he told her he was looking and did not promise. His public 'I am not arresting her. I am walking to Taravan beside her, with the law in her hand' then becomes the payoff.

Where: the bell at the cairn. This includes Bindu's 'She's retired. She doesn't need it. He did.' and Meera telling Jassi the goat is 'under your roof, which is the roof of a man who's looking after her.' What's wrong: it is unclear whose bell this is, where the small one went, and who keeps Badami. What to change: replace these lines with one clean line, or two at most, that name all three facts. This is Badami's big bell. Jassi's small kid bell lies with Sunni. Badami is kept by a named keeper, for example at his sister's apricot orchard as Jassi planned in chapter 3. Pick one keeper consistent with earlier chapters and name them. Use no unclear 'her' or 'a man'.

Where: the hinge, about a thousand words in which the jogini voice, the unequal hands, Asha's knot, the cut rope end, the grandfather's gloves, Kiran's silence, Ila's map and the queen all arrive. What's wrong: it is overloaded, and five gestured threads pull weaker than two sharp ones. What to change: keep the jogini speaking through the cold whole, with the Old Bargain unpaid and the pass closing after the fourth winter. Then sharpen two threads only, and reduce the rest to a single glance or cut them.

Where: 'I know what your father said.' What's wrong: it reads like a missing line. What to change: either have Rohan say the gloves detail aloud, his grandfather's gloves found laid neatly on a flat stone, so it lands as a possible precedent of payment (C14), or cut the exchange.

Where: Meera's 'cold with a fear no mountain had put there' about Kiran. What's wrong: the fear is vague. What to change: make it one concrete thought, for example that the Bargain is made on a rope, and her brother survived a rope that was cut. Otherwise cut it.

Where: the unequal carved hands, Asha's knot, the cut rope end, Ila's map and the queen. What to change: compress these to at most one brief image or line each, or cut them. Keep a glance at the carved hands (C06) if it fits, and keep Ila's map as a single line at most.
Keep unchanged: the walk past the eight spans and back ('Every step of it she chose'), and the final exchange, 'Nothing's watching them now... You'll have to take my word.' / 'I do.'

errors: 1 major continuity errors remain after 1 fix round(s): ch 19: Chapter 19 falls on day 12 of twenty: Sunni dies at dawn after the day-11 arrival. Nimmi says the Fair is 'four days' off, but chapter 21 (day 15) says five days remain and chapter 22 (day 16) says four, so the count goes up. Chapter 19's 'third day' door rule also cannot fit. Counted from the day-12 patrol, the doors would shut around day 15, yet chapter 21 has the rule biting only after they leave on day 17. A sixth-day rule and eight days to the Fair fit every later chapter.

2 major continuity errors remain after 2 fix round(s): ch 25: Varun was assigned as Meera's rope partner in ch 2 and walked behind her up the gully in ch 3, so he knows her face as Jassi's second. In ch 25 he asks 'Who is the woman?' and the narration says 'He did not know her'. He should not know she is the Salt Fox, but he should recognise her.; ch 26: Meera tells her bound partner 'I'm well' while believing she is dying of cold, and says it to be believed. Nothing happens, and the narration says the mountain 'had no jurisdiction over well'. The bible defines a lie as a statement believed false and said to be believed. It also says the rule is never suspended in a crisis.

beta.summary: A distinctive, emotionally exact enemies-to-lovers book: the lie-cold rule turns every confession into a costly act, and the payoffs in chapters 30 to 32 land the way readers hope. A continuity error, a thaw question that chapter 31 answers a chapter early, and a few on-the-nose lines are worth one short revision round before release.
